gen_risks.description: Delay in obtaining budget confirmation and approval from HM Treasury could postpone programme start.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage Treasury early, secure provisional approval, build contingency timeline and alternative funding arrangements.
gen_risks.evidence: timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury

gen_risks.description: Insufficient availability of skilled staff and resources within DfE and the education sector may hinder delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop recruitment plan, allocate training budget, use temporary contracts, monitor staffing levels.
gen_risks.evidence: availability of skilled staff and resources, in both DfE and the education sector

gen_risks.description: The internal CRM system may not be ready by the November 2025 MVP target, affecting school onboarding.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt agile development, set clear milestones, consider interim manual processes, allocate additional IT resources.
gen_risks.evidence: develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum-viable product from November 2025

gen_risks.description: Schools may provide food that does not meet required school food standards, risking compliance breaches.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide clear guidance, conduct audits, offer training, enforce penalties for non‑compliance.
gen_risks.evidence: Food provided must be in line with school food standards

gen_risks.description: Actual school participation and pupil attendance may be lower than forecast, reducing benefit‑cost ratio.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement outreach campaigns, monitor uptake early, adjust funding incentives, provide support to low‑take‑up schools.
gen_risks.evidence: gradual increase in school participation, supported by typical staffing patterns

gen_risks.description: Physical space constraints in schools could limit ability to deliver 30‑minute supervised breakfast provision.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct space assessments, provide technical estate advisers, fund modest facility adaptations where needed.
gen_risks.evidence: technical estate advisers to test what schools can do to mitigate any space constraints

gen_risks.description: NSBP schools may experience gaps when transitioning to FBC in September 2026, disrupting provision.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create transition plan, align timelines, provide interim support, monitor continuity of service.
gen_risks.evidence: It is anticipated that most schools on the NSBP will transfer to the FBC programme in September 2026

gen_risks.description: Complexity and confusion around the mainstream funding model could deter schools from joining.
gen_risks.mitigation: Simplify communication, produce clear guidance notes, run webinars, offer helpdesk support.
gen_risks.evidence: variation by disadvantage levels was deemed to be complicated... resulting in confusion

gen_risks.description: The call‑centre pilot for data collection may not achieve required performance, limiting data quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Pilot with clear KPIs, allocate sufficient staffing, have fallback manual data entry process.
gen_risks.evidence: call‑centre pilot to support data collection

gen_risks.description: Local authorities may lack capacity to effectively support schools, affecting programme delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide additional funding, training, and clear responsibilities to local authorities, monitor performance.
gen_risks.evidence: fund local authorities to support schools and the wider system to effectively deliver free breakfast clubs

gen_risks.description: Delay or amendment to the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill could postpone the mandatory duty.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain liaison with legislative team, prepare interim guidance, adjust rollout schedule if needed.
gen_risks.evidence: Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state‑funded schools

gen_risks.description: Start‑up grant costs may exceed the £1,000 estimate, leading to budget overruns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set up cost monitoring, allow contingency fund, review actual start‑up expenses early.
gen_risks.evidence: £1,000 start‑up grant to cover one‑off costs

gen_risks.description: Evaluation may not deliver timely insights, limiting ability to adapt programme.
gen_risks.mitigation: Define clear evaluation milestones, ensure independent commissioner has resources, integrate interim findings into management decisions.
gen_risks.evidence: evaluation will adopt an iterative, mixed‑methods approach... interim and final reporting to inform ongoing policy development

gen_risks.description: Procurement of additional advisers under the education and children’s social care framework may be delayed, reducing support for complex schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Accelerate procurement timeline, use fast‑track procedures, maintain a shortlist of pre‑qualified suppliers.
gen_risks.evidence: procurement process to increase the number of advisers supporting schools through the educational and children's social care framework

gt_risks.description: Lower value for money compared to the 'do minimum' option in year 1, due to the shorter funding period available for the preferred option's new cohorts of schools.
Delivery risks around staffing and food costs for schools newly onboarded to the free breakfast clubs programme.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated through early adopter (EA) scheme insights and support funding.

gt_risks.description: Uncertainty in the labour-market benefits (parental workforce participation gains) the programme is expected to deliver.
gt_risks.mitigation: Addressed through conservative assumptions in the economic modelling.
